articles.title: Radiographic and clinical outcomes following modified L-reverse joint-preserving osteotomy for grade II hallux rigidus: A minimum 5-year follow-up.
articles.authors: Poggio D, Fontanellas A, Ledermann G, Vega R, Torner P, Segur JM, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with prospective data collection
articles.population: Patients with grade II hallux rigidus (stiffness of the big toe joint)
articles.outcomes: Radiographic measures (metatarsal length, joint angle, joint space width) and patient-reported function using Manchester-Oxford Foot Questionnaire
articles.take_home: A joint-preserving surgical technique using a modified L-reverse osteotomy improved symptoms and pain scores in patients with moderate hallux rigidus, with stable radiographic improvements lasting at least 5 years. Three patients needed further surgery.
